title: Settings card: 2025 KTM 300 EXC / XC-W
ig_caption:
2025 KTM 300 EXC and 300 XC-W. Same manual, same stock numbers, so this one is for both. About 160 lb, fast, hard enduro, stability and grip the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the standard settings from KTM's 2025 owner's manual for the 250 and 300 EXC and XC-W.

Stock is 15 and 17 on the fork, 15 clicks and 2 turns on the shock, 15 on shock rebound, 110 mm of rider sag. Dialed went 3 clicks in on fork comp, 5 in on fork rebound, 5 in on low-speed, half a turn in on high-speed and 3 in on shock rebound. Sag stays at 110. Five clicks is a big move, so if it feels harsh in the rocks, come back toward stock two clicks at a time.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

What's your 300 running for the gnarly stuff?

title: Settings card: 2024 Kawasaki KX450
ig_caption:
2024 Kawasaki KX450. About 205 lb, fast, hardpack moto, stability and jump support the goals. Left is stock from the 2024 KX450 owner's manual, right is the baseline Dialed built for that rider.

Fork comp 12 to 11, fork rebound 12 to 10. Shock low-speed 11 to 9, high-speed 2 turns to 1 1/4, rebound 13 to 12. Sag set at 105 mm. A heavier, fast rider on the stock springs gets a little more hold everywhere, with the biggest move on high-speed for the landings.

title: Settings card: 2024 Husqvarna FC 250
ig_caption:
2024 Husqvarna FC 250. About 190 lb, fast, rutted clay moto, stock suspension, stability and jump support the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the standard settings from the 2024 Husqvarna FC 250 owner's manual.

Stock is 12 and 18 on the fork, 15 clicks and 1 1/2 turns on the shock, 15 on shock rebound, 105 mm of riding sag. Dialed kept fork comp, went 7 clicks in on fork rebound, 5 in on low-speed, a quarter turn in on high-speed and 2 in on shock rebound. Seven clicks is a big move: if the front starts to pack in the ruts, come back toward stock two at a time. Fork air: set it from the manual for your weight.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

title: Settings card: 2022 Kawasaki KX250
ig_caption:
2022 Kawasaki KX250. About 175 lb, comfortable pace, hardpack moto, stock suspension, stability and comfort the goals. This is the baseline Dialed built, next to the stock settings from the 2022 KX250 owner's manual.

Stock is 12 and 11 on the fork, 10 clicks and 1 1/2 turns on the shock, 15 on shock rebound. Dialed went 2 clicks out on fork comp, 1 out on fork rebound, 2 out on low-speed and 1 in on shock rebound, and set sag at 103 mm. Comfort was the goal, so compression came out on both ends.

All counted out from fully closed. Starting points riders refine on the bike, one change at a time.

title: Comment answer: no clickers on an older bike
ig_caption:
Someone in the comments rides a 1984 XR200R and asked what the app can do for a bike with no clickers. Fair question, and the answer is: more than you'd think.

Older bikes skip the clickers, not the tuning. Sag, fork oil level, oil weight, fork height and springs all still move. Same rules: one change at a time, write it down, ride it.
